animations.title: One set of curves and durations
animations.now: JS uses (.2,.8,.2,1), (.4,0,.2,1), (.4,0,1,1); CSS adds bare ease, ease-out, (.22,.7,.3,1), (.3,1.6,.5,1). Durations are bare numbers in 40+ places.
animations.verdict: Appeal comes from one set of named curves used everywhere. FAM's are softer than the skill's and scattered, so like things don't move alike.
animations.notes: The skill's step 4, Name the numbers: durations, curves and springs live in named tokens at the top of the file and every animation uses them. Today the Motion module declares three curves (EASE = cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) for appearing, EASE_IO = (.4,0,.2,1), EASE_IN = (.4,0,1,1)) and several functions fall back to the bare 'ease-out' keyword (press squeeze, burst, popMessages, badge, swapIcon), which the skill calls too weak to read as a decision. CSS has its own: sheets (.2,.8,.2,1), toast (.2,.8,.2,1), notif (.2,.8,.3,1), nextup (.22,.7,.3,1), voice search (.22,.7,.3,1), tabPop (.3,1.6,.5,1) overshoot, loaders (.2,1.3,.4,1) overshoot, plus 'ease' on many colour/opacity fades (fine for colour per the skill). Proposal: a :root block of --ease-out/--ease-in/--ease-in-out and --dur-* tokens, mirrored as Motion.EASE/Motion.DUR so WAAPI and CSS read the same values. Option A adopts the skill's curves as they are; B keeps FAM's feel but names it; C uses the skill's curves for movement and FAM's softer one only for large spatial moves (player, screens). Whatever is chosen, the reduced-motion rule and the 450ms cap stay. Every later slide in these decks is written in the skill's tokens; if B wins, read 'out' as FAM's (.2,.8,.2,1).

options.why: The skill's appeal rule: one set of named curves everywhere. Ease-out (.32,.72,0,1) makes responses feel instant.

options.summary: Keep today's softer curves, but name them once and remove the bare keywords and overshoots.
options.tradeoff: Least change; keeps a softer, floatier feel the skill calls weaker for things that move.

options.name: Split by distance
options.summary: Skill curves for presses, sheets and small moves; a softer long curve kept for full-screen moves.
options.recipe: Curves library: softer quad/cubic for large moves

animations.title: Pressing any button or card
animations.now: Scales by size: 1 - 8/longest side, floor 0.90, 90ms ease-out down; release 220ms back through an overshoot to 1+(1-s)×0.3. Cards up to 30% of the screen squeeze too.
animations.verdict: Right idea, two misses: small buttons go below the 0.95 floor, and the overshoot is a bounce. Wide cards should tint, not scale.
animations.notes: Skill, Anticipation, the everyday form: buttons, icon buttons and chips scale to 0.96 on press (never below 0.95) with a 150ms ease-out transition, so letting go mid-press glides back. Surfaces wider than 200px (cards, rows) change background on press instead of scaling, because 4% of a wide surface is a jump. Dense controls opt out. Put the scale on a wrapper when the element already has a transform. FAM today (index.html:6146-6186): one pointerdown listener on PRESSABLE, scale s = max(0.9, 1 - 8/longest side) so a 22px icon button computes 0.64 and is clamped at 0.90 (10% - visibly squashed), a 40px button 0.80 → 0.90, a 120px pill 0.93, a 350px card 0.977. Down: 90ms 'ease-out' keyword, fill forwards. Release: waits for the down animation to finish, then 220ms through scale(1 + (1-s)×0.3) at 60% - an overshoot of up to 3%. That wait means a quick tap plays 90 + 220 = 310ms. The composite:'add' approach is good and should stay (it keeps an element's own transform). Option A is the skill's rule exactly. Option B keeps FAM's 'scaled by size' idea, which the owner chose (§292: 'about 4 px smaller'), but clamps it to the skill's 0.95-0.98 band and removes the overshoot. Option C keeps today's. Interrupt check: the skill wants the release to turn around from wherever the press is - use a transition-like reverse (animation.reverse() or a new animation from the current computed scale) instead of waiting for 'down' to finish.

options.name: Skill press 0.96
options.summary: Every button dips to 96% and glides back; wide cards and rows tint instead of shrinking.
options.tradeoff: One number for all sizes: small icon buttons move less than today, big cards stop moving.
options.why: The press confirms the tap without a bounce; no target squashes past 5%, and releasing mid-press glides back.
options.reduced: No scale; the tint stays (it is colour, not motion)

options.name: Size-scaled, clamped
options.summary: Keep 'about 4px smaller' by size, but never below 95% or above 98%, and no spring past 1.
options.tradeoff: Keeps the owner's §292 idea; still scales wide cards slightly, which the skill avoids.

options.name: Keep today's squeeze
options.summary: Today's squeeze: down to 90% on small buttons, springing back past full size.
options.tradeoff: A bounce on every press; a quick tap plays 310ms; tiny buttons squash 10%.

animations.title: Opening a screen, going back
animations.now: Push: new screen in from 100% over 320ms (.2,.8,.2,1); old drifts to -28% and dims to 0.55. Back: 260ms (.4,0,.2,1). Reduced motion: 120ms crossfade.
animations.verdict: Inside the 300-400ms page range and exits are shorter, as the skill asks. Curves are weak, and there is no swipe-from-the-left-edge back (Jakob's law on iOS).
animations.notes: Skill timing: page transition 300-400ms; exits 20-30% shorter and quieter, except things whose destination is the point, which leave the way they came (a back is exactly that). Today: push 320ms with EASE (.2,.8,.2,1), the leaving screen to translateX(-28%) and opacity .55; pop 260ms (19% shorter - just under the 20% band) with EASE_IO (.4,0,.2,1). The new screen is active and tappable from its first frame (good - FAM's rule and the skill's 'never block input'). A second change finishes the first at once (settle()), which is not 'turning around from where it is' - a back pressed mid-push jumps to the end of the push and then pops. Jakob's law: 'swiping from the left edge goes back on iOS' - FAM's native client will get that for free; the web app has no edge swipe. Option A retimes to the skill (push 340 out, back 260 out - a back is also an arrival). Option B adds the interactive edge swipe: the screen follows the finger 1:1 and a spring (0.5s, bounce 0) carries the release velocity - flick > 0.1px/ms goes back. Option C is a quieter cross-push (24px nudge + fade, 240/180) for the many in-app pushes that aren't hierarchical. Reduced motion: the skill wants none at all; FAM's 120ms crossfade is a deliberate choice (rule:motion) - shown as the reduced-motion slide.

options.name: Push, skill curves
options.summary: Same push the owner picked: in from the right, back to the right, on the skill's ease-out.
options.tradeoff: Small change in feel; still no edge swipe.

options.name: Push + edge swipe back
options.summary: As A, plus drag from the left edge to go back: the page follows the finger and springs home or away.
options.tradeoff: Most work: a gesture recogniser beside horizontal rails, which must not steal their swipes.
options.why: People expect iOS's edge swipe; the drag is direct and a flick finishes it, and it turns around mid-way.
options.reduced: Swipe still works; the page jumps instead of springing

options.name: Short cross-push
options.summary: The new screen fades in from 24px to the right while the old fades out - quieter and quicker.
options.tradeoff: Loses the sense of a stack you can go back down; reads lighter on many pushes a session.

animations.title: Switching tabs
animations.now: Old content slides 18px and fades in 110ms, then new content slides in 200ms after a 90ms delay; the tab icon pops 420ms with a (.3,1.6,.5,1) overshoot.
animations.verdict: Tabs are fired many times a session: the skill says the new state shows on the next frame. The pop is a bounce on navigation icons, which the skill rules out.
animations.notes: Skill question 1, Frequency of use: 'Many times a session, or from the keyboard (shortcuts, arrow keys, ⌘K, tabs, focus moving) → no transition. The new state shows on the next frame.' Press feedback is exempt and keeps its 100-150ms. Today a tab change costs 110ms (old out) + 90ms delay overlap + 200ms (new in) ≈ 290ms before the page is still, and the icon plays a 420ms overshooting pop (tabPop, scale .7 → 1.15ish). Every switch also replays the pop. The owner picked 'slide by position' in §292 (rule:motion: 'tabs nudge toward the new tab's side'), so this is a deliberate reversal for the owner to make: option A follows the skill; option B keeps a sense of place with something that moves in place (the active marker glides 220ms io under the new tab - a 'moving in place' animation) while content is instant; option C keeps the nudge, shortened and on skill curves, with the pop's overshoot removed. Icon swap recipe says 'never on permanent navigation icons', so none of the options pops the icon.

options.name: Instant, press only
options.summary: The new tab is there on the next frame; the only motion is the button's own press.
options.tradeoff: Reverses the owner's §292 pick; the app feels faster but loses the sideways cue.
options.why: The skill's rule for many-times-a-session: motion stops informing by the tenth switch. Saves ~290ms per switch.

options.name: Marker glides, page instant
options.summary: Content is instant; the copper marker behind the icon glides to the new tab.
options.tradeoff: One small motion per switch, in the bar, not the page; the eye goes to the content anyway.

options.name: Nudge, shortened
options.summary: Keep the sideways nudge toward the new tab, faster, with no gap and no icon bounce.
options.tradeoff: Keeps the owner's pick in spirit; still a motion on every switch.

animations.title: Sheets and modals
animations.trigger: open / close a sheet, menu or popup
animations.now: Overlay fades and the card lifts 14px in 200ms (.2,.8,.2,1) by keyframes; closing fades and drops 8px in 150ms. Bottom sheets and centred modals move the same way.
animations.verdict: Times are right, but keyframes can't turn around mid-open, and the skill splits the two: a modal scales from 0.97 quietly; a sheet slides fully from its edge.
animations.notes: Skill recipes. Modal: 220ms in, 160ms out, opacity 0→1 and scale 0.97→1, overlay on the same clock; never slide a modal in, grow it from 0 or bounce it. Drawer and sheet: 280ms in, 200ms out, sliding all the way back to its edge because where it goes is the point; contents arrive with it in one piece; slides on a transition, never keyframes, because people close drawers mid-open; a sheet people drag uses a spring (0.5s, bounce 0) and dismisses on a fast flick (>0.1px/ms) even when it has barely moved. FAM today (2116-2129): @keyframes mo-in/mo-lift on .active, mo-out/mo-drop on .closing held 150ms by a MutationObserver. Both the bottom sheets (queue, share, ⋯ menus, Length/Voice pickers) and the centred modals (sources, confirmations) use the same 14px lift. Because they are keyframes, closing mid-open restarts the closing keyframe from the open pose (a jump); Inert: confirm `inert` is set on the closed overlay so focus can't land in it while it fades. Popovers anchored to a trigger (a tile's ⋯ menu if it is anchored) should follow the popover recipe: 160/120ms, scale .95 from the trigger with a 4px nudge. Option A splits them per the skill; B adds drag-to-dismiss on sheets; C keeps today's single look but as transitions.

options.name: Skill split
options.summary: Sheets slide all the way up from the bottom; centred popups fade in from 97% size. Both turn around mid-way.
options.tradeoff: Sheets travel further than today's 14px lift; they read as physical layers.

options.name: Split + drag to dismiss
options.summary: As A, and a sheet can be pulled down: it follows the finger, a flick closes it, the top rubber-bands.
options.tradeoff: Gesture code on every sheet; scrolling content inside a sheet must hand over at its top.
options.why: Phones teach pull-down-to-close; the skill's sheet recipe is a dragged spring with a flick, and it never blocks input.

options.name: Today's lift, interruptible
options.summary: Keep the 14px fade-and-lift for everything, but as transitions so closing mid-open turns around.
options.tradeoff: Smallest change; sheets still don't say they came from the bottom edge.

animations.title: The bottom line and the banner
animations.trigger: an action finishes; a notification arrives
animations.now: The line fades in 200ms and rises 8px from scale .98 in 220ms; its copper dot grows 260ms after 60ms. The banner drops from -140% in 280ms (.2,.8,.3,1).
animations.verdict: Close to the toast recipe. Missing: a 16px rise from its edge, an exit 20-30% shorter, Undo kept 5s, and swipe-away on the banner.
animations.notes: Skill toast recipe: 240ms in, 170ms out, rising 16px from its screen edge with a fade and leaving the same way; stacked toasts shift with transform on the same curve; swipe-to-dismiss uses a spring; a toast with an action (Undo, Retry) stays at least 5s. Errors: anything reversible gets Undo instead of a confirmation - the item leaves at once and the request goes out when the Undo window closes. Today .toast/.snack (2391-2415): opacity .2s ease and transform .22s (.2,.8,.2,1) from translateY(8px) scale(.98); the copper dot scales 0→1 over .26s after .06s - a secondary action that ends 100ms after the main one, inside the skill's 150ms. The exit is the same transition reversed (220ms) - should be ~170ms with the ease-in curve. .notif (2420-2454): translateY(-140%) → 0 over .28s (.2,.8,.3,1), opacity .2s; it is tappable. The skill also asks the scale-in to start at 0.95/0.97 (it does: .98) and never from 0 - the dot does start at 0, which is fine for a 7px dot (it reads as a point appearing). Options: A the recipe straight; B adds follow-through (the dot settles 30ms after the card with a soft spring) and swipe-away; C makes Undo visible as a draining hairline (linear, the motion is time itself).

options.summary: Rises 16px from the bottom as it fades in, leaves the same way a bit faster; Undo stays 5s.

animations.title: Opening and minimising the player
animations.trigger: tap a tile; tap the down arrow
animations.now: A copy of the tapped picture grows into the player's in 380ms while the player fades in 240ms; minimising shrinks it into the mini thumb in 340ms. The copy animates left/top/width/height.
animations.verdict: The right shared-element move, in the 300-400ms range. Fix: animate transform only (FLIP), and since it travels on both axes by >40px the skill wants an arc.
animations.notes: Skill: page transition / shared-element move / something flying to a new place: 300-400ms. Properties: movement and size changes use only transform and opacity; never animate width/height/top/left - use FLIP (measure, then animate the transform). Arcs: when something travels between two points that differ on both axes by more than 40px, move it on a curve that bulges 10-20% of the distance; for depth, scale up to at most 1.3 at the top of the arc with a larger shadow. Replacements: something that's travelling stays one element for the whole move - FAM does this (a ghost carries the picture, the real one is hidden until it lands, then the ghost fades 120ms). Today (6038-6070): ghost from the tapped picture's box to #playerBg's box over 380ms EASE via place() = left/top/width/height/borderRadius - layout every frame, which can stutter while the player screen is building. Close (6055-6070): 340ms EASE_IO into #nowThumb, player fades out 200ms, mini bar fades in 200ms after 140ms. Option A: same choreography as FLIP - the ghost is positioned at the destination box and animated with transform: translate/scale from the source box, border-radius via clip-path inset(round) - identical look, compositor-only. B adds the skill's arc: x on ease-out, y on ease-in in nested wrappers (techniques: arcs in CSS), with a shadow fading in at the midpoint. C (quiet): no flight - the player pushes like a screen and the picture blurs up in place.

animations.now: Rises from behind the tab bar in 260ms (.2,.8,.2,1), clipped so it never covers the tabs; drops back in 200ms. Its progress line animates width linearly every 200ms.
animations.verdict: Good: exit 23% shorter, origin from where it lives. Fixes: progress should be scaleX, and the thumbnail can settle a beat after the bar (follow through).

Exit is 23% shorter (inside 20-30%). The progress fill (.nowbar-fill, 2029): width 0-100% with transition: width 200ms linear, updated every 200ms - a layout property animated constantly while audio plays; replace with transform:scaleX(p) and transform-origin:left. Follow through (skill): 'when a container stops, the non-text parts inside it settle a beat later: a toast's icon, a sheet's grabber' - the thumbnail could arrive 30ms after the bar with a softer spring, overshoot under 4%. Not for text.

options.recipe: Drawer and sheet (edge it lives at)
options.tradeoff: Small visual change; mostly a performance fix for the progress line.

animations.title: Play and pause
animations.now: Old icon shrinks to 0.5 and fades in 90ms; THEN the new icon pops 0.5 → 1.1 → 1 in 180ms (90ms delay). 270ms in sequence, with an overshoot.
animations.verdict: The skill's icon-swap recipe: both icons at once, deep scale 0.3→1 with a 3px blur, spring 0.35s with no bounce. Sequential swaps double the wait.
animations.notes: Recipe 'Icon swaps': icons that change with state (play and pause, copy and check, like and liked) cross-fade through a deep scale - scale 0.3 → 1 (a timid 0.8-0.9 reads as a glitch), opacity 0 → 1, blur 3px → 0, on a spring with no bounce {duration 0.35, bounce 0} because icons aren't toys; without Motion, render both icons stacked in one grid cell and swap classes, cross-fading with cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0, 1) over ~300ms - nothing unmounts, both directions animate. Replacements: 'animate both at once; never wait for the old one to finish leaving.' Today (6343-6365): the new icon is in the button at once (good - state first) but drawn at delay 90ms after the old copy's 90ms exit, and it overshoots to 1.1. One transport rule (rule:transport): setPlayState redraws all four players - the swap must run on whichever is on screen, as now (onActive). Option C makes it instant: play/pause is a high-stakes control where the audio itself is the feedback.

options.name: Icon swap recipe
options.summary: Play and pause cross at the same moment: one shrinks and blurs away while the other grows in.
options.tradeoff: Shorter and smoother than today; loses the little pop.
options.why: Both at once halves the swap; the deep scale reads as a swap, and no bounce on a transport control.

options.name: Cross-fade in one cell
options.summary: Both icons stacked; a 300ms cross-fade with a small scale, nothing unmounts.
options.tradeoff: Gentler; the skill warns shallow scales can read as a glitch.

options.name: Instant
options.summary: The icon changes on the frame of the tap; the button's press and the sound are the feedback.
options.tradeoff: Plainest; nothing says 'swap' beyond the press.

animations.title: The episode's title settling
animations.now: The writer's title replaces the derived one with a left-to-right wipe, clip-path 320ms (.4,0,.2,1). The words are the new ones from the first frame.
animations.verdict: A good use of a mask, and words never wobble. Retime to the skill's io curve; a 2px blur bridge is the alternative when two titles look unrelated.
animations.notes: Rule title-from-content: a derived title first, then swapped for the writer's <<TITLE:>> once known; titleOverridden never replaced. Motion.retitle (6388): sets textContent first, then animates clipPath inset(0 100% 0 0) → inset(0) over 320ms EASE_IO - reveal-only, so the old title is never seen once the new is known (the §298 note). Skill: masks and reveals - clip-path gives crisp edges, a wipe goes from inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0). Cross-fades: when two states look disconnected, a 2px blur during the change bridges them. Replacements: both at once in one grid cell. Text never lags or wobbles (follow-through rule) - all three options keep the text rigid. The mini bar title (8797) runs the same wipe.

options.name: Wipe, io curve
options.summary: Keep the left-to-right wipe the owner picked, on the skill's move-in-place curve.
options.tradeoff: Almost unchanged; the wipe is noticeable on long titles that wrap.
options.why: The wipe says 'this was written for you' without moving the words; only the curve changes.

options.name: Blur bridge
options.summary: The old title blurs out as the new one sharpens in, in the same spot.
options.tradeoff: Softer; shows the old title for 220ms, which §298 chose not to.

options.name: Roll up
options.summary: The old title rises out 8px as the new one rises in under it, both at once.
options.tradeoff: Reads as 'updated'; moving text twice per episode.

animations.title: Pictures landing
animations.now: A picture that arrives 100ms+ after its tile blurs up: 8px blur, scale 1.12, fade, to sharp in 320ms. Pictures already on the device appear at once.
animations.verdict: Correct instinct - only late pictures animate. A 12% scale is a lot of movement on a tile people are aiming at; blur 8px is within the 20px limit.
animations.notes: Doherty: reads show what the person saw last time, then reconcile - FAM does: only an image whose load lands >=100ms after data-drawn animates (6405-6410), so a cached picture never pretends to load. The movement: opacity 0→1, blur 8→0, scale 1.12→1, 320ms EASE. The skill: blur under 20px (fine); entrances' softest form is fade + 8px rise + 2px blur; an image's scale on a tile someone is about to tap moves the target. Background pictures (player, reel) are held at frame one until loaded and given up after 8s - good. Many pictures land at once on a rail, so the blur-up runs on several tiles together - that's fine because each lands when it arrives, not on a stagger. Option B 'colour first' adds a placeholder in the picture's dominant colour (computed server-side when the thumbnail is made) so the tile is never empty, then cross-fades.

options.name: Gentler blur-up
options.summary: Same blur-up, smaller: soft and 4% large to sharp, a little quicker.
options.tradeoff: Less visible; still clearly 'just arrived'.
options.why: Keeps the owner's pick and the honest only-if-late rule while the tile barely moves under a thumb.

options.name: Colour first
options.summary: The tile shows the picture's main colour at once; the picture fades in over it when it lands.
options.tradeoff: Needs a dominant colour per thumbnail from the server; no blur at all.
options.reduced: Picture appears at once over the colour

options.name: Today's blur-up
options.summary: Today's: 8px blur and 12% large to sharp in 320ms.
options.tradeoff: The most noticeable; the tile grows under the finger.

animations.title: Captions advancing
animations.trigger: each sentence as it is voiced
animations.now: Each sentence arrives with ccIn 320ms ease (y 4→0, fade) and the last leaves with ccOut 320ms ease (fade, y 0→-4).
animations.verdict: Captions are read while they move and change many times a minute: keep the move tiny, exits shorter, and never the bare ease on something that moves.
animations.notes: Captions publish each sentence as it is voiced (rule live-captions). The panel marks the current sentence (mark.cc-now) and a leaving one (.cc-leaving). Skill: exits 20-30% shorter than their entrance; text never lags or wobbles; never animate anything read while it moves (squash rule) - a 4px rise is acceptable because it ends before reading starts. 'Many times a session → no transition' argues for option C, a highlight that moves through the text with no movement at all (colour is fine at 150ms ease). Under reduced motion today: no animation (1431).

options.name: Rise, shorter exit
options.summary: New sentence rises 4px into place; the last leaves faster upward, both at once.
options.tradeoff: Close to today, tidier; still moves every sentence.

options.name: Highlight only
options.summary: All recent text stays put; the spoken sentence turns full colour and the last one dims.
options.recipe: Frequency of use (colour is not motion)
options.tradeoff: Calmest to read; a new sentence appearing at the bottom has no entrance cue.
options.why: Captions change every few seconds: colour carries 'now' with nothing moving under the eyes.

options.name: Today's ccIn / ccOut
options.summary: Today's 320ms fade-and-rise in, 320ms fade-and-rise out.
options.tradeoff: Exit as long as entrance; bare ease on a move.

animations.title: Save, like and VIBE!
animations.now: Icon dips to .8 then pops to 1.2 (380ms); a copper ring grows .4→1.7 and six sparks fly out (450ms); 'SAVED' slides in beside it and stays ~1.1s.
animations.verdict: Exactly the reel's 'Check + sparkle' card - which the skill keeps for rare moments. A few times a session, the sparkle starts delaying; save the burst for the first time.
animations.notes: Skill, Secondary action: 'Only on top of a primary motion, never alone. It starts with the primary or up to 100ms after, ends within 150ms of it, and moves at most a third as much. Example: the check draws in, then a ring scales from 1 to 1.4 while fading out. Only in the rarely branch of question 1.' Exaggeration: only where a moment must register - a first success. Peak-end: save celebration for real milestones; routine completions get a quiet confirmation. Today celebrate() (6189-6236) runs on every save/like/vibe the listener turns on: icon scale 1 → .8 (20%) → 1.2 (60%) → 1 over 380ms (an anticipation dip + overshoot), ring scale .4 → 1.7 fading over 450ms, six 4px sparks travelling 0.8 × icon size over 450ms, label 1100ms linear with a ±8px slide. It never runs when the server paints state (good: setSaved/setEchoed don't call it). Options: A quiet - the icon-swap recipe (outline → filled, spring .35s) with the word beside it; B first-time only - the full burst the first time each kind is turned on (stored per device), A afterwards; C keep the burst but to the skill's numbers (ring 1 → 1.4, no dip, sparks end with the icon).

options.name: Quiet swap + word
options.summary: The outline icon swaps to filled, and 'SAVED' fades in beside it for a moment. No ring, no sparks.
options.tradeoff: Calm; loses the moment of delight the owner asked for.
options.reduced: Icon fills at once; the word shows without moving

options.name: Burst the first time
options.summary: The full ring and sparks the first time you save, like or vibe; the quiet swap after that.
options.tradeoff: Delight once per kind per device; a returning listener may never see it again.
options.why: The skill keeps secondary actions for rare moments: a first save is a peak, the twentieth is routine.

options.name: Burst, skill numbers
options.summary: Keep it every time, tightened: no dip, ring 1→1.4, sparks end within 150ms of the icon.
options.tradeoff: Keeps the owner's pick; still sparkles on the tenth save today.

animations.title: Adding to and removing from the queue
animations.trigger: Add to Queue; remove a row
animations.now: A thumbnail flies to the queue button in 450ms on a keyframed bend, shrinking; the button bumps 1.3 and the badge pops from 0. A removed row slides left 180ms, THEN the gap closes 200ms.
animations.verdict: Make it mean something, done right (it leaves toward where it went). Over the 400ms ceiling, layout properties, the shrink loses depth, and the removal runs in sequence.
animations.notes: Skill Arcs: both axes > 40px → curve bulging 10-20% of the distance; for depth scale up to at most 1.3 at the top with a larger shadow, so it lifts off the page instead of sliding across it. Staging: chain motions - 'the image reaches the cart, then the badge bumps' - FAM does exactly that (badge waits 450ms). Timing: something flying to a new place is 300-400ms; today 450ms (EASE_IO) via left/top/width/height. Numbers: a changing number rolls only the digits that change, upward when it grows, tabular-nums. Removal (removeRow, 6582): slide to -45% + fade in 180ms EASE_IN, then height/padding/margin collapse in 200ms after 180ms - two layout properties, and sequential. The skill's exits recipe: grouped exits (list items) close the gap with transforms while the item leaves (popLayout). Undo: a queue removal is reversible → bottom line with Undo for 5s (Errors: recover). Options: A arc with lift + digit roll, transform-only, 360ms; B 'drop in': the thumb drops into the queue icon like into a slot (clip as it crosses the opening - masks technique), C quiet: no flight; the queue button's count rolls up and the button bumps.

options.name: Arc with lift
options.summary: The thumbnail lifts, arcs to the queue button and lands; the count rolls up by one.
options.tradeoff: Same story as today, inside the ceiling; FLIP transform code replaces the left/top flight.
options.why: The arc and lift say 'thrown into the queue'; chaining the count after the landing keeps one motion at a time.

options.name: Drop into the slot
options.summary: The thumbnail arcs over and drops into the queue icon, clipped at its edge as if posted in.
options.spec: 380ms · arc 12% · clip at the icon edge
options.recipe: Masks: putting something into a slot
options.tradeoff: Most charming, most fiddly; the icon is small, so the slot effect is subtle at phone size.

options.name: Count only
options.summary: Nothing flies; the queue button bumps and its number rolls up.
options.tradeoff: Quietest; 'where did it go?' is answered only if the button is on screen.

animations.title: When an episode ends
animations.now: The card of four tiles fades up 12px from 98.5% over 360ms (.22,.7,.3,1), as a keyframe. A copper bar at the top empties over 15s before the first auto-starts.
animations.verdict: Countdown drawn as a draining bar is right (linear: the motion is time). The card is a modal-sized layer: 220ms, and its four tiles are copies of one element - stagger the first few.
animations.notes: Rule post-episode-grid: four recommendations, the first auto-starts in 15s; the lead is Go Deeper's own suggestion; a search box above Back stops the countdown. The card arrives with nextup-in var(--nextup-fade, 360ms) cubic-bezier(.22,.7,.3,1) - deliberately twice the old arrival so it reads as the episode handing over (comment at 2830). Skill: modal 220ms in; menus/modals/toasts 300ms or less; stagger copies of one element 30-50ms, first 6 only; the softest entrance pairs an 8px rise with a 2px blur. Peak-end: the end of an episode is the 'end' people remember - this is the place for the calmest, most legible arrival, not a flourish. The countdown bar (.nextup-timer) is transform-origin:left - good (scaleX). Option C keeps today's slower arrival because the owner tuned it on purpose.

options.name: Card, then tiles
options.summary: The card fades up, then its four tiles arrive 40ms apart; the bar starts draining once all are in.
options.tradeoff: More motion at the end of an episode; still well under half a second.
options.reduced: All appear at once; the bar still drains

options.name: Soft rise, lead first
options.summary: One soft rise with a 2px blur clearing; the lead tile's own bar shows the 15s left.
options.tradeoff: Moves the timer onto the lead tile, which makes clear which one will play.
options.why: A calm, readable end (peak-end) and the timer sits on the thing it will start - one element breaks the pattern.
options.reduced: No rise; the bar still drains

options.name: Today's handover
options.summary: Today's slower 360ms rise, kept on purpose so it feels like a handover.
options.tradeoff: Over the 300ms the skill allows a card; a keyframe that can't be interrupted.

animations.title: The FAM intro on opening
animations.now: 1.8s every open: the F and M fold into the A (420ms), the chevron charges copper→yellow twice (560ms), then the page slides off left (480ms) onto the app underneath.
animations.verdict: A choreographed rare moment within the 2.5s the skill allows - the first time. Played on every open, by the tenth it is 1.8s between the listener and their app.
animations.notes: Owner's sketch (§201): four beats, ~1.8s; the screen underneath is switched before the first frame, so it is 'a picture over an app that is already there' - nothing waits on it, but nothing can be reached either until it slides away. Skill question 1: 'Rarely: a milestone the person won't repeat this session → may be choreographed: each move up to 500ms, the whole sequence up to about 2.5s.' Each beat obeys (240, 420, 560, 480). The question is frequency: on every open it is the 'many' branch across days. Tenth use: run it at full speed as someone seeing it for the tenth time today - cut or shorten the one that starts to feel slow. Storyboards: a 3+ stage sequence should be written as a TIMING object with a comment (FAM_INTRO_CHARGE_MS is a start). Options: A full intro on first run and after sign-in only, a 500ms version otherwise (logo fade + slide); B full intro at most once a day; C keep.

options.name: Full once, short after
options.summary: The full fold-and-charge on first run and sign-in; every other open, the mark fades and slides away.
options.tradeoff: The brand moment becomes rarer; daily listeners get to the app 1.3s sooner.
options.why: Choreography is for milestones; on the hundredth open it is a delay. The short version keeps the mark.

options.name: Once a day
options.summary: The full intro the first time the app opens each day; straight in after that.
options.spec: 1.8s first open of the day · else 0ms
options.tradeoff: A daily ritual fits a daily-edition product; still 1.8s every morning.

options.name: Every open (today)
options.summary: Today's 1.8s intro on every open.
options.tradeoff: Strongest brand repetition; the most waiting.

animations.title: Sign-up's steps
animations.now: Words slide 24px and fade (out 160ms, in 260ms after 80ms); three bars at the top fill from scaleX .3 to 1 in 260ms with the appear curve.
animations.verdict: Goal gradient done right in spirit. The skill: a step bar grows from its last value from the left edge on ease-in-out, never jumps back, and a finished step shows done.
animations.notes: Skill, Zeigarnik and goal gradient: show where they are and what's left ('Step 2 of 4'), count work already done (a step finished shows as done; progress never reads 0% once they've done something); a step progress bar grows from its last value with scaleX from the left edge (never width), on the ease-in-out curve, and never jumps backward. Today: three separate bars, each filling .3 → 1 when it turns on (260ms EASE), transform-origin? (.motion-steps i - check: the fill starts at 30% because it is a scale from the centre unless origin is left). Exits: 160ms vs 260ms entrance = 38% shorter (beyond the 20-30% band - fine, quieter). One decision per step (Hick) - FAM's three steps are the sign-up form, name and picture, interests. Option C turns the three bars into one continuous bar with 'Step 2 of 3' in words (Miller/Zeigarnik).

options.name: Bars grow from the left
options.summary: Each bar fills from its left edge on the move-in-place curve; finished bars stay full.
options.tradeoff: A precise fix; the words' slide stays as the owner picked it.
options.why: Progress should read as growth from where you were, on the in-place curve, never from the middle.

options.name: Bars + step words
options.summary: As A, plus 'Step 2 of 3' under the bars, rolling to the next number on Continue.
options.tradeoff: One more line of chrome on a short flow.

options.name: One continuous bar
options.summary: A single bar that grows a third per step, starting a third full because the account already exists.
options.tradeoff: Loses the three-part count; gains 'you're already a third done'.

animations.title: The tour's spotlight
animations.now: The spotlight moves by transitioning top/left/width/height 380ms (.2,.8,.2,1); the card moves by top; the progress fill animates width.
animations.verdict: A rare, choreographed flow, so 380ms is fine. Layout properties make it stutter; the spotlight and card are two halves of one object and should share a clock.
animations.notes: Tour once per account, Skip on any card (§594-595). The hole is a box with a 9999px box-shadow scrim; it transitions top/left/width/height at 380ms - layout each frame. The card transitions top 380ms. The track's fill transitions width. Skill Properties: never animate width/height/top/left; open with FLIP; progress bars grow with scaleX from the left. Origin: paired elements (tooltip and arrow, drawer and backdrop) share one duration and one curve - hole and card do (380ms both), keep that. Options: A the same tour drawn with transforms: the hole is a fixed-size element scaled and translated (or clip-path on the scrim), card translateY; B adds staging: the hole moves first, then the card follows 80ms later and its text staggers in (heading, copy, actions 80-100ms apart - distinct pieces of a section); C cuts the moving spotlight: each step fades the scrim and card in place.

options.name: Same tour, transforms
options.summary: The spotlight and card glide exactly as now, drawn with transforms, on one clock.
options.tradeoff: Same look, smoother on phones.
options.why: A once-per-account flow should be its smoothest; only the drawing method changes.

options.name: Spotlight, then card
options.summary: The spotlight lands first; the card follows and its heading, text and buttons arrive in order.
options.tradeoff: Richer for a rare moment; about 300ms more per step.

options.name: Cross-fade steps
options.summary: No travelling spotlight: each step's scrim and card fade in where they belong.
options.tradeoff: Loses the sense of the light moving across the app.

animations.title: Reduced motion and the theme switch
animations.now: With Reduce Motion on, screens cross-fade 120ms and sheets fade in 120ms; the rest is still. Switching theme lets every colour transition run at its own speed.
animations.verdict: The skill turns every animation off under reduced motion, fades included, except things that show work is happening. A theme switch should turn transitions off for two frames.
animations.notes: Skill Verify: Reduced motion (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) - every animation is off, fades included, and every end state and every piece of information is the same as with motion on; the one exception is an indicator that work is still happening (a spinner, a progress bar), which keeps moving because a frozen spinner looks like a hang. FAM's rule:motion deliberately keeps a 120ms crossfade for screens and a 120ms sheet fade - the owner's choice in §292. Check: the search loading steps' pulse (famStepPulse) and the loading dots are turned off under reduced motion (2346-2349) - by the skill's exception, the indicator that work is happening should keep moving (a calm opacity pulse is fine). Theme switch recipe: add .theme-switching { transition: none !important } to every element for the frame the theme changes, remove it two frames later; setTheme (11418) does not, so the tab bar (200ms), switches (160ms), side buttons (all .15s) and others each fade at their own speed. Switch the theme: no colour transitions fire across the page.

options.name: Skill: all off
options.summary: Reduce Motion turns every animation off, fades included; only loading indicators keep a gentle pulse.
options.tradeoff: Reverses the 120ms crossfade the owner kept; loaders start pulsing again under the setting.
options.why: People who ask for reduced motion asked for none; a frozen loader looks like a hang, so that one keeps moving.
options.reduced: This option is the reduced mode

options.name: Today's 120ms fade
options.summary: Keep the 120ms screen crossfade and sheet fade; fix only the theme switch.
options.tradeoff: Fades are motion to some people; keeps the owner's decision.
options.reduced: This option is the reduced mode

options.name: Fade only for layers
options.summary: Screens change instantly; only sheets and modals fade 120ms so a layer doesn't appear from nothing.
options.tradeoff: A middle path; still a fade under the setting.
